theme: 3 terms on working with mixed types: a type for anything, checking a type and casting to a specific type

terms.definition: A type that can hold a value of any type, so one array can mix numbers and text.
terms.example: Use `[Any]` here, because the array holds both numbers and text.

terms.definition: A way to check the type of a value, or to treat it as another type, using `is` and `as?`.
terms.example: Use type casting to check whether this value is a `String` first.
terms.code:
let value: Any = "Swift"
print(value is String)

terms.definition: A way to treat a value as a more specific type with `as?`, which gives nil if the cast fails.
terms.example: Use downcasting to get an `Int` out, and handle nil if it fails.

quizzes.question: In this code, what is it called when `as?` tries to treat `value` as an `Int` and gives nil if it fails?
quizzes.code:
let value: Any = "Swift"
let n = value as? Int

quizzes.question: In this code, which type lets `items` hold an `Int` and a `String` together?
In this code, what is it called when `is` checks whether `value` is a `String`?
quizzes.code:
let value: Any = "Swift"
let ok = value is String

video.description:
Learn to talk about mixed types in Swift: Any, Type Casting & Downcasting, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Any - A type that can hold a value of any type, so one array can mix numbers and text.
Type Casting - A way to check the type of a value, or to treat it as another type, using `is` and `as?`.
Downcasting - A way to treat a value as a more specific type with `as?`, which gives nil if the cast fails.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.description:
Explain Any, Type Casting & Downcasting in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Any, 타입 캐스팅, 다운캐스팅 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Any - A type that can hold a value of any type, so one array can mix numbers and text.
한국어: Any: 어떤 타입의 값이든 담을 수 있는 타입

Type Casting - A way to check the type of a value, or to treat it as another type, using `is` and `as?`.
한국어: 타입 캐스팅: `is`와 `as?`로 값의 타입을 확인하거나 다른 타입으로 다루는 방법

Downcasting - A way to treat a value as a more specific type with `as?`, which gives nil if the cast fails.
한국어: 다운캐스팅: `as?`로 값을 더 구체적인 타입으로 다루는 방법, 실패하면 nil

In this video, Mina and Jake sort an array of mixed values and learn how to check and cast each one, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

dialogue.title: The mixed array

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mina, my `data` array has numbers and text. Which type can hold both?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So Any means any type at all?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. But then you must check the type before you use a value.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. Type casting checks a value with `is`, like `first is String`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So type casting only checks? I thought it changes the value.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: To get an `Int` out, use downcasting: `first as? Int`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Downcasting gives nil, so use `if let` to stay safe.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Got it. Any is flexible, but I will use downcasting carefully.

dialogue.code:
let data: [Any] = [42, "Mina", 3.5]
let first = data[0]
let isText = first is String
let number = first as? Int
